verdict_reason: I independently re-derived the Leinster magnitude and magnitude-dimension formulas: on a fresh 37x7 cloud over 97 scales, BLME matched Magnipy's Cholesky path to max absolute 2.13e-14 and max relative 8.91e-16, and on an irregular six-point line it matched the closed form to 2.02e-16 relative error. The full point-cloud implementation is nevertheless not completely faithful to Euclidean geometry: for a deterministic 40x9 standard-normal cloud from default_rng(343), I used the next 9 RNG draws as a normalized direction and translated every point by the same norm-1e8 vector; this created 6 false zero distances while all 10/10 ladder rungs passed the range and monotonicity guards. Versus cancellation-resistant pdist, magnitude_dimension moved 1.578329 to 2.273549 (+44.0%), magnitude_area_norm moved 0.595619 to 0.565990 (-4.97%), and magnitude_high_scale moved 39.999954 to 33.999962 (-15.0%).
comparable_reason: Only magnitude_area_norm is close to cross-model comparable, with a numerical-stability caveat: rescaling one fixed cloud by factors 1e-4, 1e-2, 1, 7, 100, and 1e4 left it at 0.608141841061 with absolute span 3.33e-16, and zero-padding d=9 to 64, 512, and 4096 changed it by 0.00e+00. In a fresh local 20-model panel its Spearman correlations were rho=+0.167 with d_model (p=0.483), -0.126 with n_layers (p=0.597), +0.222 with log parameters (p=0.347), and +0.087 with vocabulary (p=0.715), max |rho|=0.222 versus 0.276 for raw magnitude_area. The other first-class outputs are not architecture-clean: magnitude_auc had rho=+0.761 with vocabulary (p=9.71e-5), while magnitude_dimension had rho=+0.557 with log parameters (p=0.0107); the shared distance helper also moves the normalized value by 4.97% under the deterministic translation isometry above.
github_reason: I ran the clean local Magnipy checkout at commit 7d49b90f110db42fe666ada2964fea020d2cb1dd on identical inputs. Across 97 scales on a 37x7 cloud, BLME versus the released Cholesky implementation had max absolute error 2.13e-14 and max relative error 8.91e-16; the maximum-secant magnitude dimension was exactly 1.479522415273089 in both implementations, and the duplicate-inclusive median heuristic was exactly 1.154700538379252 in both.
paper_reason: Limbeck et al.'s Figure 1 reports scaled MagArea approximately 133, 99, 69, and 48 for X1-X4. With NumPy seed 0 and the released tutorial generator, the author code gave 143.345951, 111.169729, 85.163035, and 61.465918 (7.78%-28.1% above the figure because the released X1 generator is not seed-pinned), and BLME's kernel on that exact author grid matched all four to max absolute 1.42e-14. BLME's emitted per-cloud-window quantity n*magnitude_area_norm instead gave 24.450752, 20.441533, 10.046569, and 31.845854, errors of 81.6%, 79.4%, 85.4%, and 33.7% and the wrong X1>X2>X3>X4 ordering, so only the computational kernel, not the published-number protocol, is reproduced.
confounds_reason: The fresh 20-model current-code panel confirms architecture association in the raw ladder summaries: magnitude_auc versus vocabulary had Spearman rho=+0.761 (p=9.71e-5), and magnitude_dimension versus d_model and log parameters had rho=+0.517 (p=0.0197) and +0.557 (p=0.0107). The explicit normalized area did not retain or move that association in the same panel: all four tested architecture correlations had |rho|<=0.222 and p>=0.347, but this does not make the task's remaining emitted columns architecture-free.
defects: CODE: src/blme/tasks/geometry/magnitude.py:137-147 forms squared distances as ||x||^2+||y||^2-2x.y, which catastrophically cancels for translated coordinates. On the default_rng(343) 40x9 cloud, using the next 9 RNG draws as a normalized direction for a shared norm-1e8 translation, it created 6 false zero pairs and max pair-distance relative error 1.00; all 10/10 guards still passed while magnitude_dimension changed 1.578329 to 2.273549 (+44.0%).

CODE: src/blme/tasks/geometry/magnitude.py:215-257 drops bad ladder rungs and integrates over whatever noncontiguous domain remains, while only _meta_n_scales discloses the changed domain and that key is excluded from analysis at lines 336-339. For the deterministic cloud X[i,j]=sin((i+1)(j+1))+0.1*i+0.03*j translated by +1e8 in every coordinate, only 2/10 rungs survived, yet the task emitted magnitude_auc=1.337919 rather than failing closed; the stable-distance value was 10.804914 (-87.6%).

PROTOCOL, not implementation verdict: src/blme/tasks/geometry/magnitude.py:272-315 hard-codes a separate per-cloud cutoff 10/median(distance), whereas the paper defines a shared evaluation interval from a 95%-cardinality convergence scale. On the four released paper clouds, BLME's cutoffs were only 0.0413-0.1492 of each 95%-convergence scale and reached only 10.4%-35.6% of cardinality, so the comment that this is where magnitude has essentially converged is false and the emitted magnitude_area is not the paper's MagArea protocol.

COMPARABILITY, not implementation verdict: the 20-model local panel found magnitude_auc rho=+0.761 with vocabulary (p=9.71e-5) and magnitude_dimension rho=+0.557 with log parameters (p=0.0107). These raw columns must not be treated as architecture-free even though their formulas are faithfully implemented.

PAPER PROVENANCE: the released tutorial does not seed X1 before sampling it. With an explicit seed 0, official scaled MagArea was 143.345951/111.169729/85.163035/61.465918 rather than the Figure 1 readouts 133/99/69/48, relative differences 7.78%-28.1%; exact figure reproduction needs the authors' original realized cloud or RNG state.
